Source: Tesouro Nacional, FINBRA (to 2012) and SICONFI (from 2013), as
served by Base dos Dados (`basedosdados.br_me_siconfi`, tables
`municipio_despesas_funcao`, `uf_despesas_funcao`,
`municipio_receitas_orcamentarias`), queried on 2026-10-15 (SQL in
`_scripts/sql/2026-10-15-siconfi-extraction.sql`). Raw extracts:
`_data/raw/siconfi/siconfi_*_amz_*.csv`, nine Legal Amazon states.
Consumer: the descriptive sprint script `_scripts/09-descriptive-data.R`
(task 4.5); promoted to the pipeline under task 4.8.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
options(width = 120)
```

```{r read}
raw_dir <- "_data/raw/siconfi"
ct <- cols(.default = col_character(), ano = col_integer(), valor = col_double())
exp_m <- bind_rows(
  read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "siconfi_municipio_despesas_funcao_amz_2000_2003.csv"), col_types = ct),
  read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "siconfi_municipio_despesas_funcao_amz_2004_2024.csv"), col_types = ct))
exp_u <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "siconfi_uf_despesas_funcao_amz_2000_2024.csv"), col_types = ct)
rev_m <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "siconfi_municipio_receitas_orcamentarias_amz_2000_2024.csv"), col_types = ct)
exp_munic <- read_rds("_data/interim/siconfi_expenditure_munic_2000_2024.rds")
exp_uf <- read_rds("_data/interim/siconfi_expenditure_uf_2013_2024.rds")
rev_munic <- read_rds("_data/interim/siconfi_revenue_munic_2000_2024.rds")
panel <- read_rds("_data/final/panel_amz_2000_2020_final.rds")
sample_geo <- panel %>% distinct(geocode, state_abbreviation)
six <- c("Saúde", "Educação", "Assistência Social", "Previdência Social", "Gestão Ambiental")
totals <- c("Despesas por Função", "Total Geral da Despesa por Função",
            "Despesas (Exceto Intra-Orçamentárias)", "Despesas (Exceto Intraorçamentárias)",
            "Despesas Exceto Intraorçamentárias")
```

## Q1. What do the four extracts contain?

What is checked: rows, years, municipalities or states, stages, and the
share of rows carrying the Base dos Dados account id (expenditure) or
the Tesouro account code `portaria` (revenue).

```{r q1-shape}
bind_rows(
  exp_m %>% summarise(file = "municipal expenditure", rows = n(), years = paste(range(ano), collapse = "-"),
                      units = n_distinct(id_municipio), stages = n_distinct(estagio_bd),
                      id_share = mean(!is.na(id_conta_bd) & id_conta_bd != "")),
  exp_u %>% summarise(file = "state expenditure", rows = n(), years = paste(range(ano), collapse = "-"),
                      units = n_distinct(sigla_uf), stages = n_distinct(estagio_bd),
                      id_share = mean(!is.na(id_conta_bd))),
  rev_m %>% summarise(file = "municipal revenue", rows = n(), years = paste(range(ano), collapse = "-"),
                      units = n_distinct(id_municipio), stages = n_distinct(estagio_bd),
                      id_share = mean(!is.na(portaria))))
exp_u %>% count(estagio_bd)
```

**Finding.** The municipal expenditure extract holds the nine states'
808 municipalities for 2000-2024 under one stage (empenhadas), with the
function id present from 2004; the state table begins in 2013 (five
stages, all years to 2024); the revenue extract holds the matched
accounts 2000-2024, with the Tesouro code filled from 2013 and absent
before (FINBRA names only) and on the total rows.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-15-c (expenditure), D-2026-10-15-d (revenue):
the stage, the periods and the keys named here.
**Assertion.** `09-descriptive-data.R`, raw-state block (stage, states,
808 municipalities, years, unique keys).

## Q2. Which rows give a municipality's total and its functions, year by year?

What is checked: the total rows by name and year, the 2010-2012 pair of
total rows under the same id, the 2013 rows without id, and the sum of
the function rows against the published total.

```{r q2-totals}
exp_m %>% filter(conta %in% totals) %>% count(ano, conta) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ano, values_from = n) %>% select(conta, `2004`, `2009`, `2010`, `2012`, `2013`, `2014`, `2016`, `2017`, `2024`)
pair <- exp_m %>% filter(ano %in% 2010:2012, conta %in% totals[1:2]) %>%
  select(id_municipio, ano, conta, valor) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = conta, values_from = valor)
pair %>% summarise(n = n(), equal = sum(abs(`Despesas por Função` - `Total Geral da Despesa por Função`) < 1),
                   median_ratio = median(`Total Geral da Despesa por Função` / `Despesas por Função`))
fun_sum <- exp_m %>%
  mutate(kind = case_when(conta %in% totals[-2] ~ "total", conta == totals[2] ~ "drop",
                          str_detect(conta, "^Despesas") ~ "intra", TRUE ~ "function")) %>%
  filter(kind %in% c("total", "function")) %>%
  group_by(id_municipio, ano, kind) %>% summarise(v = sum(valor), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = v)
fun_sum %>% filter(ano >= 2004) %>% group_by(ano) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), within_1pct = mean(abs(`function` / total - 1) < 0.01), max_ratio = max(`function` / total)) %>%
  mutate(across(-c(ano, n), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

**Finding.** From 2004 every reporting municipality-year has one total
row (`Despesas por Função` to 2012, the "exceto intraorçamentárias"
total under three spellings from 2013); 2010-2012 repeat the total under
`Total Geral da Despesa por Função`, equal in 2,106 of 2,204 cases and
dropped. The function rows sum to the published total within one
percent in every year from 2004, so the 2002-2003 totals, which have no
published row, are taken as the sum of the 28 functions.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-15-c.
**Assertion.** `09-descriptive-data.R`, raw-state block (one total row
per municipality-year from 2004) and output block (function sum never
above the total).

## Q3. How complete is the municipal reporting, overall and in the sample?

What is checked: municipalities with a total (or any function row before
2004) by year, the 502 sample municipalities by year and state, and the
municipalities missing most often.

```{r q3-coverage}
cov <- exp_munic %>% mutate(in_sample = geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% summarise(all_9_states = n(), sample = sum(in_sample), .groups = "drop")
cov %>% pivot_longer(-year) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = value)
cov %>% filter(year >= 2002) %>%
  transmute(year, sample_pct = round(100 * sample / nrow(sample_geo)),
            rest_pct = round(100 * (all_9_states - sample) / (n_distinct(exp_munic$geocode) - nrow(sample_geo)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-year) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = value)
exp_munic %>% semi_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>% filter(year %in% 2004:2020) %>%
  count(state_abbreviation, year) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n) %>%
  left_join(sample_geo %>% count(state_abbreviation, name = "n_sample"), by = "state_abbreviation") %>%
  relocate(n_sample, .after = state_abbreviation)
sample_geo %>% left_join(exp_munic %>% filter(year %in% 2004:2020) %>% count(geocode, name = "years_reported"), by = "geocode") %>%
  mutate(years_reported = replace_na(years_reported, 0L)) %>% count(years_reported) %>% arrange(years_reported) %>% head(8)
```

**Finding.** Reporting is incomplete in every year: between 388 (2008)
and 500 (2022) of the 502 sample municipalities have a total, with the
worst years 2004-2008 and 2012 and the gaps concentrated in Pará,
Maranhão and Amazonas. The 306 non-sample municipalities of the nine
states report at nearly the same rate in every year (a few points
higher before 2017), so the gaps are FINBRA's voluntary reporting, not
a property of the sample; from 2017, when SICONFI became mandatory,
coverage is above 98 percent. The gaps are the source's; the descriptive
displays show them as missing municipality-years and the aggregates are
computed over reporting municipalities, never imputed.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-15-c (no imputation).
**Assertion.** none; the coverage is reported, not asserted.

## Q4. Are the five functions comparable across the 2002 and 2013 breaks?

What is checked: the pre-2002 vocabulary, the share of reporting
municipalities with each function present (post-2013 files list only
non-zero functions, so absent means zero), and the sample medians per
capita by year.

```{r q4-functions}
exp_m %>% filter(ano %in% 2000:2003) %>% distinct(ano, conta) %>% count(ano, name = "n_functions")
exp_m %>% filter(ano %in% 2000:2001) %>% distinct(conta) %>% pull(conta) %>% sort()
present <- exp_m %>% filter(ano >= 2002, conta %in% six) %>% distinct(id_municipio, ano, conta) %>%
  count(ano, conta) %>% left_join(exp_munic %>% count(year, name = "reporting"), by = c("ano" = "year")) %>%
  mutate(share = round(n / reporting, 3)) %>% select(ano, conta, share) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = conta, values_from = share)
present %>% filter(ano %in% c(2002, 2005, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2017, 2020, 2024))
exp_munic %>% semi_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>% filter(year %in% 2002:2024) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(c(exp_health_pc_brl_2024, exp_education_pc_brl_2024, exp_social_assistance_pc_brl_2024,
                              exp_social_security_pc_brl_2024, exp_environment_pc_brl_2024, exp_total_pc_brl_2024),
                            ~ round(median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .names = "{str_remove(str_remove(.col, 'exp_'), '_pc_brl_2024')}"),
            .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** 2000-2001 use the fifteen-function classification that
preceded Portaria 42/1999 (`Saúde e Saneamento`, `Educação e Cultura`,
`Assistência e Previdência`), which does not map onto the five
functions, so the function series start in 2002 and only the total is
kept for 2000-2001. Health, education and social assistance are present
for almost every reporting municipality in every year; social security
(own pension regimes) and environmental management are present for a
minority after 2013, which the absent-as-zero rule treats as zero
spending. The sample medians per capita rise without a visible step at
2013: health from about R$ 340 in 2004 to R$ 1,060 in 2020, education
from R$ 590 to R$ 1,390, social assistance from R$ 49 to R$ 138,
environmental management from zero to R$ 12 (2024 reais; per capita is
NA in 2000-2001 and 2023-2024, outside the interpolated population).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-15-c: functions from 2002, absent functions in a
reporting year are zero.
**Assertion.** `09-descriptive-data.R`, output block (function columns NA
only before 2002).

## Q5. What does the state table cover?

What is checked: years and states, the total row by year, the five
functions, and the state governments' social spending per capita beside
the municipal aggregate of each state.

```{r q5-states}
exp_u %>% filter(estagio_bd == "Despesas Empenhadas", conta %in% c(six, totals)) %>%
  count(conta, ano) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = ano, values_from = n)
exp_uf %>% filter(year %in% c(2013, 2016, 2020, 2024)) %>%
  select(state_abbreviation, year, health = exp_health_pc_brl_2024, education = exp_education_pc_brl_2024,
         assistance = exp_social_assistance_pc_brl_2024, environment = exp_environment_pc_brl_2024) %>%
  mutate(across(-c(state_abbreviation, year), round)) %>% arrange(year, state_abbreviation) %>% filter(year == 2020)
munic_agg <- exp_munic %>% filter(year == 2020) %>% group_by(state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(munic_social_pc = round(sum(exp_social_brl_2024, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(population, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
exp_uf %>% filter(year == 2020) %>% transmute(state_abbreviation, state_social_pc = round(exp_social_pc_brl_2024)) %>%
  left_join(munic_agg, by = "state_abbreviation") %>%
  mutate(munic_share = round(munic_social_pc / (munic_social_pc + state_social_pc), 2))
```

**Finding.** The Base dos Dados state table begins in 2013, so the
state-government series (nine states, every year to 2024, all five
functions present) covers 2013-2024 only; the FINBRA state files for
2000-2012 are not in Base dos Dados and would have to come from the
Tesouro site. In 2020 the municipal aggregate of health, education and
social assistance per capita is of the same order as the state
government's, with the municipal share of subnational social spending
between 0.29 (Acre, Amapá, where the state government spends most) and
0.67 (Maranhão), so display D2 can be drawn for 2013-2020.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-15-c: state series 2013-2024; the 2000-2012
state gap is an open follow-up (task 4.5).
**Assertion.** `09-descriptive-data.R`, raw-state and output blocks (nine
states, 2013-2024, complete function columns).

## Q6. Do the revenue items chain across the three account plans?

What is checked: the family totals by year under the rules of script 09
(FINBRA names to 2012; Tesouro codes of the 2013-2017, 2018-2021 and
2022-2024 plans, parent level only), the parent-against-children
equalities that justify reading the parent, the share of reporting
municipalities with a zero in each item, and the cases where the total
is below current transfers.

```{r q6-revenue}
rev_munic %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(c(rev_total_brl_2024, rev_current_brl_2024, rev_transfers_current_brl_2024,
                              rev_union_transfers_brl_2024, rev_fpm_brl_2024, rev_sus_brl_2024, rev_fundeb_brl_2024,
                              rev_fnde_brl_2024, rev_fnas_brl_2024),
                            ~ round(sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e9, 2),
                            .names = "{str_remove(str_remove(.col, 'rev_'), '_brl_2024')}"), .groups = "drop")
chk <- function(parent, children, years) {
  p <- rev_m %>% filter(ano %in% years, portaria == parent) %>% group_by(id_municipio, ano) %>% summarise(p = sum(valor), .groups = "drop")
  k <- rev_m %>% filter(ano %in% years, str_detect(portaria, children)) %>% group_by(id_municipio, ano) %>% summarise(k = sum(valor), .groups = "drop")
  inner_join(p, k, by = c("id_municipio", "ano")) %>%
    summarise(parent = parent, years = paste(range(years), collapse = "-"), n = n(), equal = sum(abs(p - k) < 1))
}
bind_rows(
  chk("1.7.1.8.03.0.0", "^1\\.7\\.1\\.8\\.03\\.[1-9]\\.0$", 2019:2021),
  chk("1.7.1.3.00.0.0", "^1\\.7\\.1\\.3\\.(50|51|99)\\.0\\.0$", 2022:2024),
  chk("1.7.1.1.51.0.0", "^1\\.7\\.1\\.1\\.51\\.[1-9]\\.0$", 2022:2024),
  chk("1.7.1.8.05.0.0", "^1\\.7\\.1\\.8\\.05\\.[1-9]\\.0$", 2018:2021),
  chk("1.7.1.4.00.0.0", "^1\\.7\\.1\\.4\\.(50|51|52|53|99)\\.0\\.0$", 2022:2024),
  chk("1.7.2.4.00.00.00", "^1\\.7\\.2\\.4\\.(01|02|99)\\.00\\.00$", 2013:2017))
rev_munic %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(across(c(rev_fpm_brl, rev_sus_brl, rev_fundeb_brl, rev_fnde_brl, rev_fnas_brl), ~ round(mean(.x == 0, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
                   .names = "{str_remove(str_remove(.col, 'rev_'), '_brl')}_zero"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2002, 2005, 2010, 2013, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2024))
rev_munic %>% filter(rev_transfers_current_brl > rev_total_brl * 1.001 + 1) %>% count(year)
```

**Finding.** The transfer families run continuously across the 2013,
2018 and 2022 account-plan changes, with the aggregate levels moving
smoothly (FPM, FUNDEB and SUS each grow through the period in 2024
reais, with the 2018 SUS and FNAS dips the sign of the 2018 transition
layout, when the parent rows were reported by fewer municipalities). The
parent rows read by the script equal the sum of their children wherever
both exist, which is why the script reads parents only. Zero shares are
below five percent for FPM in every year and higher for SUS and FNAS in
2018-2019; FNDE and FNAS have no line before 2002 and are NA there. Between
120 and 342 municipalities a year in 2002-2012, and 24 in 2024, carry
current transfers above the total, because the published totals are net
of the FUNDEF/FUNDEB deductions (taken from 2002) while the transfer
lines are gross, so the script asserts FPM against current transfers
rather than against the total.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-15-d.
**Assertion.** `09-descriptive-data.R`, raw-state block (unique code per
municipality-year from 2013, unique total name) and output block (FPM
non-negative and within current transfers; FNDE and FNAS NA before 2002).

## Q7. Are the per-capita values plausible in the sample?

What is checked: the distribution of expenditure and transfer per capita
in the sample municipalities, 2004-2020, and the join onto the panel.

```{r q7-plausibility}
q <- function(x) c(p1 = quantile(x, .01, na.rm = TRUE), median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE), p99 = quantile(x, .99, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
pd <- read_rds("_data/final/panel_amz_2000_2020_descriptive.rds") %>% filter(year %in% 2004:2020)
pd %>% select(exp_total_pc_brl_2024, exp_health_pc_brl_2024, exp_education_pc_brl_2024, exp_social_assistance_pc_brl_2024,
              rev_total_pc_brl_2024, rev_fpm_pc_brl_2024, rev_sus_pc_brl_2024, rev_fundeb_pc_brl_2024, rev_fnde_pc_brl_2024, rev_fnas_pc_brl_2024) %>%
  map_dfr(q, .id = "variable") %>% mutate(across(-variable, round))
pd %>% summarise(rows = n(), with_expenditure = sum(!is.na(exp_total_brl)), with_revenue = sum(!is.na(rev_total_brl)),
                 both = sum(!is.na(exp_total_brl) & !is.na(rev_total_brl)))
pd %>% filter(exp_total_pc_brl_2024 > 15000 | rev_total_pc_brl_2024 > 15000) %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation, year, population, exp_total_pc_brl_2024, rev_total_pc_brl_2024) %>%
  mutate(across(c(exp_total_pc_brl_2024, rev_total_pc_brl_2024), round)) %>% arrange(desc(exp_total_pc_brl_2024)) %>% head(10)
```

**Finding.** The sample medians sit where small Amazon municipalities
should (total spending R$ 3,100 per capita in 2024 reais, FPM R$ 890,
FUNDEB R$ 750, SUS R$ 280), the upper tail belongs to the smallest
municipalities and to the royalty recipients, and the expenditure and
revenue series join the panel on the same municipality-years (7,762 of
the 8,534 sample cells of 2004-2020 carry both).
**Decision.** none required; the tail is shown, not trimmed.
**Assertion.** `09-descriptive-data.R`, output block (row count and key
of the descriptive panel unchanged by the joins).
